requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
rationale:
I judge the two supplied tests adequate for `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`. I did not request implementation source, because the assertions are enough to map each obligation. **Main test:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts]` builds one chapter. It has an outer `:::::{cite} habeas:util` fence containing: - a metadata-only citation paragraph; - an inline citation; - a nested `{cite}` fence; - nested req, example and definition containers; - literal contexts. Outside the fence it adds an unfenced citation, a utility-only fence, an unresolved fence, an HTML-literal fence and an unclosed fence. **Secondary test:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` is marked for the display requirement and covers several container kinds. **Obligations mapped to assertions** - **Body shown as ordinary prose, with no opening badge or border.** - The main test parses the output with pulldown_cmark and asserts `

Nested prose.

` and `

Utility-only.

`. It also asserts that the ordinary paragraph with `` stays a paragraph. - It asserts that the nested fence's opening `rules.ready` badge is not in the prose. The only `rules.ready` badge left there is the inline citation, so the count is 1. - The CSS assertions require `padding: 0`, `border: 0` and a left margin of `0` on `.habeas-citation-passage`. That covers left alignment and no enclosing border. - The secondary test checks that, for `:::{cite}` openings, the opening citation and metadata citations appear only in the annotations before ``, and the opening citation appears exactly once. - **Right-gutter marker, one marker for the outermost fence.** - The main test asserts exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list` despite the nested `{cite}` fence. - The CSS assertions require `position: absolute`, `right:` and no `left:` on the marker. - The main test asserts `position: relative` on the passage. - **List contents.** - The list contains exactly 4 `
  • ` entries: `habeas:util` (opening), `rules.other` (metadata paragraph), `rules.ready` (inline and nested fence, deduplicated to one) and `rules.term_rule` (from a nested definition). - `rules.inside`, which is cited only inside the nested req and example, is absent from the list. - Those nested declarations keep their own rendering: the prose has the `aria-label` and href, and their detail chapters carry the badge. - **Links and hover text.** - The test asserts the project citation href `rules.html#habeas-req-rules.other` in the list. - It asserts `habeas-builtin" title=` for the built-in citation. - **Accessibility.** - The test asserts the summary `aria-label` and the title. - It asserts a `:focus-visible` outline rule on the summary. - The marker is a native `
    `/``, which is keyboard operable. - **Opening the list does not hide the passage.** The test asserts that the prose follows `
    ` as a sibling. - **Inline citations and unaffected contexts.** - The inline `rules.ready` citation remains a badge in the prose. - An unfenced citation before the fence keeps its badge and href, and no list appears before the passage. - Utility-only, unresolved, unclosed, HTML-literal and code-fenced contexts keep their original text and rendering. - **No source mutation.** The test asserts the guide file on disk is unchanged. It also asserts that `text_references` returns the same result before and after rendering. The secondary test adds this coverage: multiple citations on one line, `habeas:util` hidden from visible prose, and the source and declarations unchanged across several container kinds. No obligation is left without an asserting test, and I found no marking gap.

::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
